Functional alcoholic here and I can relate to what you are saying. Don't be too hard on yourself as 25 is still young and the fact that you recognize your problem is important. The world pushes alcohol as a social tool and it is pretty much impossible to get away from it in this society. I would approach it this way. You know you have a problem so that is a win. Make sure that priorities will always come before your drinking. Job, rent, food and good health as well as relationships with others. If you can insulate your drinking to not affect those areas you are okay. The law issue sounds like disrespect for others and might not necessarily be the drinking. You may want to investigate that on its own. Try to do social things with your peers and if they are not drinking try to emulate them or if they are drinking try to match their pace and just slow down. The idea is to have fun but even if you know that once you go home you can drink all you want. People will say drinking alone is bad but that is bullshit as most people drink alone. Create a routine you enjoy wnd maybe plan things like I will have these beets then cook myself supper.

I have lived with this addiction my entire life. It is a daily struggle and you have to see it that way. If you can go a week without right on. If you binge a couple days in a row no shame just try a little harder. Diets dont work and this is the same create little changes here and there and overall the entire situation will get better. Don't get bogged down by the huge obstacle but see it as small individual steps. I have gone from drinking almost every day to about once a week. I allow myself that once a week binge and feel mo shame. Sometimes things are tough and I might drink 2-3 a week but once again no shame just try to reign it in again.

Trust me it will be a daily battle but once you start focusing on positives like your health, money you saved, not feeling hung over and better social interactions you will gain strength and it will all get easier. Just try to move forward in a positive way and only good can come from that. Good luck.
